evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep skips the framing entirely. Opens with 'Do you have a few moments to go over that?' and immediately begins probing phone number and email without the 10–15 minute time-box or 'dependable quote' promise.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks 'before I go over the details are there any specific concerns or questions that you would like answered on this call?' but only after confirming contact info. Customer responds with scope and flat hourly rate question, which the rep then addresses before full discovery.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises multiple concerns: small couch angle/awkwardness upstairs (rep acknowledges with 'Understood'), furniture list and prep strategy (rep follows with 'are we moving any mattresses?', 'any large TVs?', 'anything else?'), walkability/access (rep confirms 'both locations' and asks about truck parking). Rep does probe deeper on each item rather than one-and-done.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Rep acknowledges items ('Okay', 'Understood', 'Gotcha') but never says 'So what I'm hearing is...' or confirms the full picture with the customer.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (house), stories (two stories/loft), rooms (implied: living room, garage), walking distance (~20 feet to door from truck), additional rooms (garage), special considerations (couch angle, squat rack, treadmill, curio cabinets with glass, propane heater, outdoor furniture). Destination address and distance also confirmed (10 minutes). All seven items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not mentioned. Rep never asks 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Not asked. No mention of typical box count or overflow check.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives range anchored to size: 'A typical move this size see the 1600 square feet usually takes between six and a half to eight and a half hours' then personalizes downward based on customer's prep level: 'I do not feel like that is going to be an accurate estimate for this move. I'm thinking we thinking between probably four and five hours.' Final estimate: '$192 an hour... budget between $768 and $960.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee / overnight fee not disclosed upfront. Pricing framing present: 'two and a half hour minimum once we go over that minimum the time is for rated in fifteen minute increments' and 'the time starts as soon as we get on site and open the contract, you then have us for as long as you need us.' Rep does not frame as 'not a guess' explicitly.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep says 'does that sound fair?' but customer immediately responds 'Okay' with no pause held. Rep fills silence: 'Yeah, and that is our value days so that's one of our better rates for the week.' No genuine silence observed.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Fully delivered. 'we do have an on time guarantee if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange immediately start discounting money of your final bill.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Fully delivered. 'we have our no worries damage coverage, which is our two free evaluation coverage that is included in the hourly rate provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No explicit 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar. Rep lists promises but does not ask confirmation or close the loop. Also mentions 'meet your mover email' which is not part of Section 5 script.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep moves directly to 'I do have availability on the thirtieth. I have an 8:30 AM to 9:00 AM arrival. Would you like us to help you with your move?' with no genuine 'What's still concerning you?' check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' before the ask.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Full. 'Would you like us to help you with your move?' asked plainly, no built-in out offered.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. No reference to rate holding or confirmation language.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirms: arrival window (8:30–9:00 AM) and moving date (September 30th). Missing: phone number confirmation, crew size details, pickup/destination addresses re-confirmed, and crew notes about customer's concerns (narrow couch, glass items, etc.). Customer defers to email confirmation: 'Can I confirm through email?' and rep agrees without capturing a phone number or full details on the call.

top_strength: Brianne gathered exceptionally thorough logistics details through natural follow-up questions, building a clear picture of the job (furniture list, access, prep level, special items) that allowed her to personalize the estimate downward from typical range.
coaching_note: Skip the opening setup entirely and lead with the Section 1 quid pro quo framing—'we have availability... this takes 10–15 minutes... you'll walk away with a quote you can depend on... does that sound good?'—before confirming contact details, and hold genuine silence after 'does that feel fair?' instead of immediately re-pitching the rate.
